questions.def: "A minority of" requires "of" before the noun.
questions.question: ___ students submitted their assignments on time.

questions.def: "Neither" refers to two options; "none" refers to more than two.
questions.question: Of the two candidates, ___ is truly qualified.

questions.def: "Number" refers to countable items like participants.
questions.question: Only a small ___ of participants attended the lecture.

questions.def: "Much" is used with uncountable nouns like "information".
questions.question: ___ of the information provided was relevant to the research.

questions.def: "Further" implies metaphorical distance or degree; "farther" is physical.
questions.question: ___ evidence suggests a link between the two events.

questions.def: "Quantity" is correct with uncountable nouns like "resources".
questions.question: A significant ___ of resources has been allocated.

questions.def: "The majority" requires "the" when referring to a specific group.
questions.question: ___ of the committee members were present at the meeting.

questions.def: "Little" suggests almost no doubt, an uncountable noun.
questions.question: There is ___ doubt about the validity of the results.

questions.def: "Sufficient" is a formal adjective meaning adequate.
questions.question: Only a ___ amount of rainfall occurred this month.

questions.def: "Several" refers to more than two, countable.
questions.question: ___ of the experiments yielded conclusive results.

questions.def: "Additional" is an adjective describing the noun research.
questions.question: ___ research is needed to confirm these findings.

questions.def: "Number" goes with countable nouns like "studies".
questions.question: An increasing ___ of studies support this hypothesis.

questions.def: "Few" implies almost none, for countable nouns.
questions.question: ___ of the participants had prior experience in this field.

questions.def: "Some of" requires "of" when referring to specific data.
questions.question: ___ the data is available for public access.

questions.def: "Amount" is used with uncountable nouns. "Contamination" is uncountable.
questions.question: Only a negligible ___ of the sample was contaminated.

questions.def: "Initial" refers to the first stage of research.
questions.question: ___ research suggests a correlation, but more investigation is needed.

questions.def: "Most of" requires "of" before a definite noun phrase.
questions.question: ___ the students completed the assignment ahead of schedule.

questions.def: "Sufficient" is an adjective describing "funds".
questions.question: ___ funds were allocated to complete the project.

questions.def: "Some" refers to a portion of the uncountable noun "equipment".
questions.question: ___ of the equipment was damaged beyond repair.

questions.def: "Considerable" means large amount of effort.
questions.question: ___ effort is needed to achieve the desired outcome.

questions.def: "Number" relates to countable nouns.
questions.question: A limited ___ of seats are available.

questions.def: "Few" implies almost none for countable nouns like "applicants".
questions.question: ___ of the applicants possessed the required skills.

questions.def: "All of" requires "of" with a specific noun phrase.
questions.question: ___ the participants agreed to the terms and conditions.

questions.def: 'A' is used before consonant sounds; 'considerable' starts with a consonant.
questions.question: ___ considerable debate surrounds the efficacy of the proposed policy.

questions.def: 'Few of' implies a small number disagreeing out of a larger group.
questions.question: ___ those present disagreed with the findings of the report.

questions.def: 'A number of' functions as a determiner followed by a plural noun.
questions.question: A ___ of studies have explored this phenomenon.

questions.def: 'The' is used to refer to a specific majority.
questions.question: ___ majority of respondents indicated a preference for remote work.

questions.def: 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns like 'evidence'.
questions.question: ___ evidence suggests a correlation between diet and health.

questions.def: 'Quantity' is the correct noun form to use here.
questions.question: Only a small ___ of the product was damaged.

questions.def: 'A' is used before 'certain' because it starts with a consonant sound.
questions.question: ___ certain level of ambiguity is inherent in the interpretation.
